problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of a continuous convex real-valued function on a second-countable real Hilbert space. A minimizer xstar exists with ‖x0−xstar‖≤R; differentiability is not required.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Stochastic subgradient oracle g(x,ω): its expectation belongs to ∂f(x). Each call uses a fresh IID seed; only the vector reply is available, without function values or the decomposition components.

distinctive_assumptions.label: heavy_tailed_noise
distinctive_assumptions.details: For each x, g(x,ω)=u(ω)+v(ω) almost surely, with E‖u‖²≤G0² and ‖v‖≤G1(f(x)−fstar) almost surely. Only a second moment is imposed on u, allowing heavy tails; neither component must be centered. This is not a uniform variance bound on the complete oracle.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The oracle magnitude has an objective-gap-dependent decomposition, implying ‖E g(x,ω)‖≤G0+G1(f(x)−fstar). Public information comprises E, x0, R, G0, G1 and ε, with R,G0,ε>0 and G1≥0. The objective, minimizer, sampling law and decomposition are hidden; no smoothness assumption is imposed.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedLipschitzConvex.lean: Public; Params; IsOracle.decomposition; spec.publicInput; spec.valid; spec.admissible

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: Return a measurable E-valued output with f(output)−fstar≤ε on the success event; no particular iterate or averaging rule is required.

accuracy.label: high_probability
accuracy.details: Failure probability P(f(output)−fstar>ε)≤1/10, jointly over algorithm randomness and IID oracle seeds, under a fixed oracle-call budget.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The convex problem uses an unusual stochastic subgradient decomposition combining a bounded-second-moment component with an almost-sure component proportional to the objective gap, allowing unbounded oracle magnitudes without smoothness.

descriptionHtml:
Stochastic Generalized Lipschitz Convex Minimization

We consider minimizing a continuous convex function f:E→R on a separable real Hilbert space E. A given point x0∈E satisfies ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R, where R>0 and x⋆ is a global minimizer. At x∈E, the oracle returns a random vector whose mean is a subgradient of f. Each reply decomposes into a component with second moment at most G02 and a component bounded almost surely in norm by G1(f(x)−f(x⋆)), where G0>0 and G1≥0. Samples are independent and identically distributed. For ε>0, the goal is a measurable output x¯∈E satisfying f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤ε with probability at least 9/10.

The optimization problem is minx∈Ef(x). Write ⟨⋅,⋅⟩ for the inner product and ∥⋅∥ for its induced norm. The algorithm receives E, x0, R, G0, G1, and ε; the objective and sampling distribution are accessed through the oracle.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Convexity and initial distance). The function f is continuous, and for every x,y∈E and t∈[0,1], f((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)f(x)+tf(y). There exists a fixed x⋆∈E such that f(x⋆)≤f(x)for every x∈E,∥x0−x⋆∥≤R.

Assumption 2 (Stochastic subgradient oracle). Let Ω be a measurable space, let ν be a probability measure on Ω, and let g:E×Ω→E be jointly measurable. For every x∈E, the map g(x,⋅) is Bochner integrable under ν, and f(x)−f(y)≤⟨Eξ∼ν[g(x,ξ)],x−y⟩,x,y∈E. At call k=0,1,…, a query x∈E receives g(x,ξk). The random variables (ξk)k≥0 are measurable, mutually independent, and each has law ν. Algorithm randomness is independent of this sample sequence.

Assumption 3 (Generalized moment bound). For every x∈E, there exist measurable maps ux,vx:Ω→E such that ∥ux(⋅)∥2 is integrable under ν and g(x,ξ)=ux(ξ)+vx(ξ)ν-a.s.,Eξ∼ν[∥ux(ξ)∥2]≤G02,∥vx(ξ)∥≤G1(f(x)−f(x⋆))ν-a.s.

After the allotted oracle calls, the algorithm must return a measurable output x¯∈E satisfying P(f(x¯)−f(x⋆)>ε)≤110, where P is the joint law of the algorithm’s randomness and the oracle sample sequence.

comparisonHtml:
Continuous convex f on a second-countable real Hilbert space with its Borel structure; a minimizer x⋆ satisfies ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R. Here R,G0,ε>0 and G1≥0. IID samples have law p and joint law P. The jointly measurable, integrable oracle g has mean in ∂f(x) and a measurable decomposition g=u+v with ∫∥u∥2dp≤G02 and ∥v∥≤G1(f(x)−f(x⋆)) almost surely. Target: P{f(x^)−f(x⋆)>ε}≤1/10.

(1): No expected-gap guarantee; larger constant. Extra logarithms lose for b≳κ2; no assured gain when log⁡(e+FG1/G0)≲ℓ3.
(3) SGD / AdaGrad-Norm (Kovalev 2026), Thms. 3–4 O(1+exp⁡(O(RG1))b+b2). Finite-dimensional setting; Markov conversion. (1): Polynomial instead of exponential dependence on RG1; improves the growth-dominated regime. (1): No expected-gap guarantee; extra logarithms in the accuracy term.
(4) Classical SGD (Nemirovski et al. 2009), Eq. (2.21) O(1+b2). Special case G1=0, finite dimension; projection onto the known R-ball; Markov conversion. (1): No established improvement on this restriction. (1): Extra log3⁡(2+b) factor; no expected-gap guarantee.

Abbr: κ=1+RG1, b=RG0/ε, ℓ=log⁡(2+κ+b); F=sup∥x−x0∥≤R(f(x)−f(x⋆)). Costs count all sampled oracle calls, including batches in (1). Markov conversion means tuning the expected gap to ε/10. (1) uses R,G0,G1,ε as tuning inputs.

import LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex

open MeasureTheory
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedLipschitzConvex

open OracleTemplate

structure Public where
  E : Type
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [linearE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [completeE : CompleteSpace E]
  [measurableE : MeasurableSpace E]
  [borelE : BorelSpace E]
  [countableE : SecondCountableTopology E]
  x0 : E
  R : ℝ
  G0 : ℝ
  G1 : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

attribute [instance] Public.normedE Public.linearE Public.completeE
  Public.measurableE Public.borelE Public.countableE

structure Params extends Public where
  Ω : Type
  [measurableΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]

attribute [instance] Params.measurableΩ

structure IsOracle {E Ω : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [MeasurableSpace E] [MeasurableSpace Ω] (p : Measure Ω)
    (f : E → ℝ) (xstar : E) (oracle : E → Ω → E) (G0 G1 : ℝ) : Prop where
  measurable : Measurable (Function.uncurry oracle)
  integrable : ∀ x, Integrable (oracle x) p
  subgradient : ∀ x y,
    f x - f y ≤ ⟪∫ ω, oracle x ω ∂p, x - y⟫
  decomposition : ∀ x, ∃ u v : Ω → E,
    Measurable u ∧ Measurable v ∧
    (∀ᵐ ω ∂p, oracle x ω = u ω + v ω) ∧
    Integrable (fun ω => ‖u ω‖ ^ 2) p ∧
    (∫ ω, ‖u ω‖ ^ 2 ∂p) ≤ G0 ^ 2 ∧
    (∀ᵐ ω ∂p, ‖v ω‖ ≤ G1 * (f x - f xstar))

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Public
  Instance q := q.E → ℝ
  Query q := q.E
  Reply q := q.E
  Output q := q.E
  publicInput q := q.toPublic
  valid q := 0 < q.R ∧ 0 < q.G0 ∧ 0 ≤ q.G1 ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q f O :=
    ∃ (g : q.E → q.Ω → q.E) (p : ProbabilityMeasure q.Ω)
      (P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → q.Ω)),
    StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID (fun k (ξ : ℕ → q.Ω) => ξ k)
      (p : Measure _) (P : Measure _) ∧
    O = { Seed := fun _ => q.Ω
          law := P
          answer := fun _ (_, x) seed => g x seed } ∧
    ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ f ∧ Continuous f ∧
    ∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧ ‖q.x0 - xstar‖ ≤ q.R ∧
      IsOracle (p : Measure _) f xstar g q.G0 q.G1
  successful q f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧ ∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧
      (P : Measure _) {ω | q.ε < f (output ω) - f xstar} ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (1 / 10 : ℝ)

end LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedLipschitzConvex
